best_for: Command-line users who would rather watch Twitch, YouTube and other live streams in VLC or mpv than in a browser tab.

points.title: A pipe, not a player
points.text: Streamlink grabs a stream and hands it to a video player you already have, such as VLC or mpv. Without a player installed it has nothing to show the video in.

points.title: One plugin per site
points.text: Support for each site comes from a plugin. The docs list about 130, including Twitch, YouTube and Dailymotion. It also has a Python API for scripts.

points.title: Windows builds bring their own parts
points.text: The Windows builds bundle an embedded Python, Streamlink's dependencies and FFmpeg for joining audio and video, so you install nothing else.

points.title: Installer or portable
points.text: The installer adds Streamlink to `PATH` and writes a config file that points at the bundled FFmpeg. The portable archive skips the config, so you set `--ffmpeg-ffmpeg` yourself. Both need 64-bit Windows 10 or later, and the installer can run for one user or all users.

points.title: Free under a BSD license
points.text: Streamlink is free software under the Simplified BSD license. There is no paid tier.

points.title: Windows only here
points.text: This listing covers Windows, with 72 versions kept. On macOS and Linux you install it from PyPI or a package manager; the project itself packages only PyPI, the Windows builds and Linux AppImages.
